name: ADUM6000ARIZ
title: ADuM6000: 5 kV isolated power converter with a selectable 5 V or 3.3 V output, up to 400 mW
summary: A complete isolated power supply in a 16-lead wide-body SOIC: an isoPower converter that moves power across a chip-scale transformer and regulates the far side to 5 V or 3.3 V, chosen by the VSEL pin. It gives up to 400 mW (5 V in, 5 V out), 330 mW (5 V to 3.3 V) or 132 mW (3.3 V to 3.3 V) at about 31% efficiency, with 5000 V rms isolation for one minute, more than 25 kV/µs common-mode transient immunity, UVLO and thermal shutdown. RCIN, RCOUT and RCSEL let one part regulate others in parallel for more power, or switch the converter off. It runs from −40°C to +105°C; the RI-16-2 package has 8.3 mm creepage, the RW-16 7.6 mm. It is aimed at powering USB peripherals, RS-232, RS-422 and RS-485 transceivers, industrial field buses and PLCs.

pins.name: VDD1
pins.function: Primary supply, 3.0 V to 5.5 V. Joined inside to pin 7; feed both from the same supply.

pins.name: GND1
pins.function: Primary-side ground. Joined inside to pin 8; connect both to the same ground.

pins.name: RCIN
pins.function: Regulation control input, used only in slave mode (RCSEL low): connect to a master isoPower device's RCOUT, or hold low to turn the converter off. With RCSEL high (master or standalone) it does nothing. A weak pull-down holds it low; in a noisy setting tie it low or drive it from a PWM source. Never hold it high while RCSEL is low: VISO then rises too far and damages the part and its loads.

pins.name: RCOUT
pins.function: Regulation control out. With RCSEL high it carries this part's PWM control signal, to be wired to RCIN of one or more slave isoPower devices that this part then regulates.

pins.name: RCSEL
pins.function: Mode select: high for standalone or master, low for slave. A weak pull-up holds it high; in a noisy setting tie it firmly high or low.

pins.name: VDD1
pins.function: Primary supply; the same node as pin 1.

pins.name: GND1
pins.function: Primary-side ground; the same node as pin 2.

pins.name: GNDISO
pins.function: Isolated-side ground. Joined inside to pin 15; connect both to the same ground.

pins.name: VISO
pins.function: Isolated supply to the loads: 5.0 V with VSEL high, 3.3 V with VSEL low. A 5.0 V output is not guaranteed from a 3.3 V primary supply. Joined inside to pin 16; connect the two outside as well.

pins.name: VSEL
pins.function: Output voltage select: tied to VISO the setpoint is 5.0 V, tied to GNDISO it is 3.3 V. A weak pull-up holds it high; in a noisy setting tie it firmly high or low. Has no effect in slave mode.

pins.name: GNDISO
pins.function: Isolated-side ground; the same node as pin 9.

pins.name: VISO
pins.function: Isolated supply output; the same node as pin 10.

circuits.title: Recommended PCB layout and bypassing
circuits.description: The converter standing alone with its supply decoupling. Each supply pin pair gets two capacitors in parallel, 0.1 µF and 10 µF: C1 and C2 across VDD1 and GND1 at pins 1 and 2, C3 and C4 at pins 7 and 8, C5 and C6 across VISO and GNDISO at pins 16 and 15, C7 and C8 at pins 10 and 9. The small one is a low-inductance ceramic. RCIN, RCOUT, RCSEL and VSEL leave the part as plain traces to be tied or driven as the mode and output voltage require.
notes: Pins 1 and 7 (VDD1), 2 and 8 (GND1), 10 and 16 (VISO) and 9 and 15 (GNDISO) are each one node inside the part.
Pins 2 and 8 and pins 9 and 15 sit on enlarged copper pads; the GND1 pad of pin 2 also covers pin 3 and the GNDISO pad of pin 15 also covers pin 14. Pins 11 and 12 are left open.
The lead length from both ends of each capacitor to its supply pin is 10 mm or less in total.
Bypassing pin 1 to pin 8 and pin 9 to pin 16 is worth adding unless the two ground pins of a side are joined close to the package.

operation.text: VDD1 drives a 180 MHz oscillator that switches current through a tiny air-core transformer built on the chip. The secondary rectifies and regulates to 3.3 V or 5 V. The controller sits on the isolated side: it makes a PWM signal and sends it back across the barrier on a dedicated iCoupler data channel, and that signal gates the primary oscillator to set how much power crosses. Inside are four silicon dies mounted on two separate paddles of one lead frame. Efficiency reaches about 31%.

RCSEL high makes the part standalone or a master: it regulates itself and puts its PWM signal out on RCOUT. RCSEL low makes it a slave whose oscillator follows RCIN, so one regulator can steer several isoPower devices. Slaves share the load evenly, and their VISO pins may be joined to act as one supply; with one feedback path there is no contention. The ADuM6000 can serve as master, slave or standalone; other family members can take only some of these roles.

In slave mode with RCIN held low the oscillator stops, VISO goes away and the supply current drops below one milliamp, so an isolated subsystem can be switched off to save power. Driving RCSEL high brings the converter back. RCIN high with RCSEL low is forbidden: the output then overshoots and damages the secondary side.

A UVLO with hysteresis watches VDD1 (and VISO): the converter starts once VDD1 passes about 2.7 V and stops only when it has fallen 0.3 V below that. The part therefore draws no current until the system supply has risen, and a dip caused by its own load current cannot switch it off and set up an oscillation. Below the threshold the primary oscillator is held off.

There is no soft start. Once VDD1 passes UVLO the primary runs flat out, because the secondary is still below its own UVLO and cannot send a control signal; full power flows until VISO reaches regulation, then PWM control takes over and the input current falls back in proportion to the load. Current and time to regulation depend on the load and on how fast VDD1 rises. A fast ramp (200 µs or less) gives a peak of up to 100 mA per volt of VDD1; a slow ramp gives a surge of about 300 mA near 2.7 V. The inrush stays below the short-circuit input current. For a 5 V output the VDD1 source must not limit below 300 mA, or the part may stall short of regulation and sit for a long time drawing heavy current at a low voltage. VISO overshoots at start-up; a clamp (a Zener diode, for instance) protects loads that cannot take it.

The supply pins carry switching noise from the 180 MHz oscillator and from the data channel. Each side needs at least two capacitors in parallel, 0.1 µF and 10 µF: the small, low-inductance ceramic for noise, the large one for ripple and regulation. Fit them between pins 1 and 2 for VDD1 and between pins 15 and 16 for VISO, with no more than 10 mm of total lead length from both ends of the capacitor to the pin.

Where large common-mode transients occur, keep board coupling across the barrier small, and arrange any coupling that remains so that every pin on one side sees the same. Uneven coupling can push the voltage between pins past the absolute maximum ratings and latch the part up or destroy it.

At full load the part dissipates about 1 W. No heat sink can be fitted to an isolator, so heat leaves mainly through the ground pins into the board. At high ambient temperature give pins 2 and 8 (GND1) and 9 and 15 (GNDISO) enlarged pads with several vias each to the ground plane; pad size is set by the room available. θJA is measured on a JEDEC 4-layer board with fine traces in still air, treating the four dies as one thermal unit with the hottest junction. In normal use the part delivers full load over the whole temperature range without derating; better ground copper adds margin at high ambient.

The 180 MHz switching drives high-frequency currents into the board's ground and power planes, which radiate from the board edges and as a dipole between the primary and secondary ground planes. A grounded enclosure is the suggested remedy; without one, lay the board out with RF practice. Application note AN-0971 covers board layout for emissions.

When the junction rises past about 150°C the PWM stops and the output current with it; below about 130°C it starts again. If VISO is shorted hard to ground, the part first draws its maximum current, set by VDD1, and dissipates it on the primary side, heats to 150°C, shuts down, cools to 130°C and restarts, cycling until the short is removed. The protection is for accidents; for dependable service keep the junction below 130°C by limiting dissipation.

Insulation wears out under voltage at a rate set by the waveform across it. Bipolar ac stresses the barrier most, and the 50-year target under bipolar ac sets the recommended working voltage of 424 V peak. Unipolar ac and dc, which never cross 0 V (either polarity), stress it far less and allow 565 V peak reinforced or 600 V peak basic while keeping 50 years. A waveform that crosses 0 V counts as bipolar. Some approved working voltages exceed the 50-year voltage, and running at them can shorten insulation life.
